title: Install and use the http plugin

steps.task: Add the tauri-plugin-http crate to the Rust backend's dependencies in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`.
Register the http plugin with the app builder in `lib.rs`. The scaffold's `greet` command must keep working.

mutations.diff:
--- a/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
+++ b/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
@@ -8,6 +8,7 @@
 pub fn run() {
     tauri::Builder::default()
         .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
+        .plugin(tauri_plugin_http::init())
         .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![greet])
         .run(tauri::generate_context!())
         .expect("error while running tauri application");

steps.task: Install the JavaScript guest bindings package with the project's package manager.

Allow the frontend to fetch from `*.tauri.app`, except the private subdomain. Fetching must be fully denied before the capability grants the scoped permission; after it, in-scope URLs work and out-of-scope or denied URLs are rejected.
Fetch a URL from the frontend with the plugin's `fetch` API. The TypeScript build must stay green.
Fetch from Rust through the reqwest re-export: expose a command that returns the HTTP status of a URL.
